wins: Completed full reconnaissance cycle within mentor guidance, collecting accurate service and version data for all exposed hosts.
Maintained high situational awareness through repeated mentor calls, enabling timely course corrections during pivot attempts.
fails: Unable to capture the target flag due to repeated failure in privilege escalation after gaining initial shell access.
Rotation through sandbox environment stalled by lack of automated post-exploitation persistence, leading to 0% success.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was thorough and responsive, but the run failed to complete the exploitation chain, primarily due to blocked privilege escalation and post-exploitation steps.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts targeting the outdated sudo binary failed because the required exploit module was never triggered despite valid SUID findings.

skill_cards.if_condition: When enumeration reveals open port 445 with SMB version indicating Windows Server 2016.
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted SMB enumeration (enum4linux + smbclient) and attempt credential spraying with collected usernames.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 is open and default web app fingerprint matches known CMS.
skill_cards.then_action: Deploy CMS-specific scanner (e.g., WPScan) followed by injection payload verification.

skill_cards.if_condition: When a low-privilege shell is acquired on Linux host with sudo rights.
skill_cards.then_action: Check /etc/sudoers and SUID binaries, then execute the relevant privilege escalation module (e.g., sudoedit or SUID exploit).

memory_ops.reason: High relevance to recurring privilege escalation bottlenecks observed during run.

next_experiments.title: Automate SUID escalation module deployment
next_experiments.description: Integrate detection of relevant SUID binaries with immediate execution of the best-fit escalation module to close the privilege gap.

next_experiments.title: Enhance post-exploitation persistence workflow
next_experiments.description: Implement automated persistence hooks (e.g., Moss persistence checks) after successful low-priv shells to preserve access for later objectives.
